memory_update.text: POWL should remain high-priority in the data-center power/interconnect stack because it has direct disclosed data-center switchgear/behind-the-meter order evidence, but later layers must test lumpiness, margin conversion, customer concentration, and whether market attention has already caught up.

MYRG is a lower-attention services/interconnection candidate: stronger as a second-order beneficiary of grid/substation/data-center electrical work than as a pure equipment bottleneck; quantify data-center C&I backlog before promotion.
AAON is a thermal-infrastructure candidate hidden inside HVAC classification; BASX and liquid-cooling disclosures are the key signal, with margin/capacity conversion as the main falsification path.

For this node, underfollowed public-market mapping should separate four subnodes: medium-voltage switchgear/packaged power, electrical construction and substations, thermal/liquid cooling, and regulated utility load-growth territories.
Still need a targeted pass on regional utilities with data-center load-growth filings and large-load tariffs; this pass prioritized equipment, services, and thermal suppliers.

node: Data-center power delivery, grid interconnection, transformers, switchgear, and thermal infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a concentrated underfollowed lane below the obvious AI-infrastructure leaders: custom medium-voltage switchgear and packaged power systems, electrical construction/interconnection services, and data-center thermal/liquid-cooling components. The strongest direct evidence in this pass is Powell Industries' disclosed post-quarter data-center order above $400M, AAON's BASX data-center/liquid-cooling backlog and sales acceleration, and MYR Group's transmission, substation, and commercial/industrial exposure to data-center projects. Vertiv is retained only as the high-attention reference anchor for the power/cooling category; the discovery lane is POWL, MYRG, and AAON. This is research support only, not a buy/sell list.
